THE SHORT ANSWER

When owners disagree about value

Two family members inherit a house and disagree about its value. Business partners own a rental home together but cannot agree on a buyout price. Or a trustee needs a defensible starting point for a property-related decision. In situations like these, the disagreement is often not just about the house—it is about which number everyone can reasonably rely on.

Clarify the valuation question

An independent residential appraisal provides a documented opinion of value based on an identified property, effective date, intended use, and appropriate market evidence. It does not decide legal rights or guarantee that everyone will agree, but it can help clarify the valuation question. For disputes involving an earlier event, a retrospective appraisal may be needed rather than a value as of today.

Define the assignment before work begins

If a dispute involves litigation or testimony, discuss those requirements upfront so the appropriate scope of work can be considered.
